newsitem.title: USA: Largest U.S. doctor's group forms ethics institute.
newsitem.headline: Largest U.S. doctor's group forms ethics institute.

text.p: The American Medical Association (AMA) said on Friday it was establishing an institute to research and train doctors on current issues of medical ethics.
The Institute for Ethics will tackle issues such as managed care, genetic testing, doctor unionization and care for the dying, officials told a news conference.
Dr. Linda Emanuel, head of the institute, said the aim was "to help reinstate ethics to its time-honoured and much-needed place as an integral part of the practice of medicine."
The institute was announced in conjunction with a two-day conference on medical ethics by the AMA, the largest U.S. physician's group.
The first major project of the institute would be a two-year effort to train doctors on care for dying patients, Emanuel said.
The project aims to reach doctors through national and regional conferences, seminars and mailings of educational materials.
It will focus on methods of managing pain and other symptoms of terminal illnesses, planning end-of-life care with patients, and dealing with the psychiatric consequences of terminal illness.
Another early project will aim to produce an "ethics report card" for all health care organisations, measuring how they comply with medical ethics guidelines.

For example, a managed care organisation could be penalised on the report card if it imposed a "gag rule" preventing doctors from discussing care options, Emanuel said. "We want the ethics standards to be met," she said.
Emanuel said the report card would be publicly released, perhaps after organisations have been given a chance to respond to and correct negative evaluations.
The institute will have four main areas of expertise: professionalism, managed care, end-of-life care and genetic medicine.
It will work in conjunction with the AMAs existing Council on Ethical and Judicial Affairs, which develops the organisation's code of ethics.
